notes: Background: Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Embeds LLM for help center chat, contextual search, and a light personalization layer in product UI.
Initial contact: interested in Hosted API to validate latency & cost for core chat flow; SE demo completed 2026-02-24.

Hosted trial summary (7-day): steady-state QPS ~12, daily peak QPS 48 (short bursts), 95th pct concurrency observed 40. Traffic diurnal with two peak windows (US east morning, US west late afternoon).
Token mix observed in trial: avg prompt tokens 120, avg completion tokens 220; overall token mix ~50% chat completions, 35% embeddings (search indexing + live lookup), 15% reranking requests.
Performance notes: median latency for Hosted API (us-east) 120ms per token for chat flows with rw-instruct-13B quant model profile; embeddings pipeline (batched) had good throughput, batch sizes 64.

Use-case priorities: 1) Improve support deflection via chat (low-latency), 2) Fast semantic search (embeddings store + online lookup), 3) Re-rank candidate results for product search (bursty but CPU-bound).

POC asks: 1) Dedicated capacity sizing estimate for steady-state + 3x peak bursts; 2) cost comparison: Hosted vs Dedicated commit at 6/12/24 months; 3) SLOs for tail latency and options for regional routing.

Security: customer requires SSO/SAML integration, audit log retention 1 year, KMS integration for key management, and ability to pin model versions. Data residency: some europe customers — prefer US-first but want roadmap for EU residency.
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable per-session latency guarantees and a clear BOM for reserve capacity. If Dedicated can halve our token cost at 80% utilization, we can justify a 12-month commit.'

SE notes: likely Dedicated sizing: 4 x A100-equivalent for chat+rerank baseline (concurrency ~40), autoscale to 8 GPUs for 3x burst; or equivalent mix of L4s with model-specific quantization. Need to run eff-perf matrix with customer prompts to refine.
Finance: initial ARR target $75k first-year; procurement cycle expects exec sign-off by end of April 2026.

Operational concerns: prefer VPC Private control plane for auditability; interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations — particularly batching and KV caching to reduce token spend on repeated context.
